narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while many had 6 or more years. This limited tenure appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while at your current company. This strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving, as having external opportunities often indicates that someone is considering or actively exploring options elsewhere.

Third, working in the “other” sector (rather than medical or education) also nudged the outcome toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees predicted to stay work in this broader category, suggesting the model sees different retention patterns across industries.

Although several positive elements exist in your profile, such as having medical insurance, no overtime demands, and general job satisfaction, these were not strong enough to outweigh the top three signals.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to accelerate your development and sense of stability. You may want to reflect on whether the external opportunities you’ve received better align with your long-term plans. Addressing these areas could improve your retention outlook in the future.
